question_text: A government office spends 18% of its annual budget on electricity. If electricity costs P216,000 yearly, what is the total annual budget?

hint_ladder.title: Orient
hint_ladder.text: This is a 'part-to-whole' percentage problem. You know the part (P216,000) and the percentage (18%), and you need to find the whole (total budget). Think of it like this: if 18% of your budget equals P216,000, what would 100% be?

hint_ladder.title: Rule
hint_ladder.text: The golden rule for these problems: Part = Percentage (as a decimal) x Whole. So here, P216,000 = 0.18 x Total Budget. To find the Total, you just divide the Part by the decimal percentage.

hint_ladder.title: Apply
hint_ladder.text: Set up the equation: 0.18 x Budget = 216,000. Now solve for Budget by dividing both sides by 0.18: Budget = 216,000 / 0.18.

hint_ladder.title: Nearly There
hint_ladder.text: Now do the division: 216,000 divided by 0.18. A quick trick: multiply both numbers by 100 to make it easier. That gives you 21,600,000 divided by 18. What do you get? That's your total budget.

A.text: P1,000,000 is a tempting wrong answer. It looks like you might have accidentally divided by 0.216 instead of 0.18. Or maybe you thought 18% was 0.216? A common slip. But remember, 18% as a decimal is 0.18, not 0.216. So the correct division is 216,000 / 0.18, not 216,000 / 0.216.

B.text: P1,100,000 is a bit too low. If you check: 18% of 1,100,000 is only P198,000, which is less than the P216,000 spent. So the total budget must be larger than this. This answer might come from a small arithmetic mistake in the division, like rounding too early.

C.text: Correct! P1,200,000 is the total annual budget. Because 18% of 1,200,000 is exactly P216,000. You got it right by dividing the part by the percentage: 216,000 / 0.18 = 1,200,000.

D.text: P1,300,000 is too high. If you check: 18% of 1,300,000 is P234,000, which is more than the P216,000 spent. So the budget can't be this big. This might happen if you accidentally divided by 0.166 (thinking 18% was 16.6%) or if you added instead of dividing.

next_time_rule: When you know the 'part' and the 'percentage,' find the 'whole' by dividing: Whole = Part / (Percentage as Decimal). For example, if P216,000 is 18% of the budget, just do 216,000 / 0.18. Always double-check by multiplying your answer by the percentage to see if you get back the part.
deconstruct_text: Let's break this down in a way that will stick with you. The problem tells us that P216,000 represents 18% of the total budget. In math language, that means: 0.18 x Total Budget = 216,000. To find the Total Budget, we need to 'undo' the multiplication by 0.18. We do that by dividing: Total Budget = 216,000 / 0.18. Now, dividing by 0.18 might look tricky, but here's a mental shortcut: multiply both numbers by 100 to turn 0.18 into a whole number. So it becomes 21,600,000 / 18. Now, 18 goes into 21,600,000 how many times? Well, 18 x 1,200,000 = 21,600,000. So the total budget is P1,200,000. The key insight here is the 'part-to-whole' relationship. You have a piece of the pie (the electricity cost) and you know what fraction of the whole pie it represents (18%). To find the size of the whole pie, you divide the piece by the fraction.
